faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.sub: Quick answers to common questions about docmd.
faq.a1: docmd is a zero-config, open-source documentation engine that converts Markdown files into production-ready documentation sites. Read the Quick Start guide →
faq.q2: How does it differ from Docusaurus or VitePress?
faq.a2: docmd requires zero configuration — no React, no Vue, no framework knowledge. See the full comparison →
faq.q3: Do I need React or a framework?
faq.a3: No. docmd is framework-free. You write Markdown, run a command, and get a production site.
faq.q4: How does the AI-first integration work?
faq.a4: docmd ships a native MCP server (docmd mcp) so AI agents can search, read, and validate your docs live. It auto-generates llms.txt and llms-full.txt context files, and docmd init creates a SKILL.md instruction file for coding agents. MCP server docs →
faq.a5: Yes. Completely free and open-source under the MIT License. View on GitHub →
faq.q6: Can I use it with my existing Markdown files?
faq.a6: Yes. Point docmd to any directory of Markdown files. Markdown syntax reference →
faq.a7: Yes. Native i18n with locale-first URLs and localized search indexes. i18n configuration →

search.hero.title:
Local Semantic Search.
Zero API keys. 100% Private.
search.hero.sub: Enable instant semantic search on your documentation site with a tiny <3KB browser runtime. Zero network dependencies, zero costs.
search.features.title: Private Semantic Search
search.features.sub: Bring modern vector search directly to your static docs without third-party services.
search.feature.local.title: Tiny Client
search.feature.local.desc: Browser runtime is under 3KB gzipped. It downloads zero model weights and runs no neural networks—performing pure arithmetic for instant hybrid scoring.
search.feature.semantic.title: Offline Indexing
search.feature.semantic.desc: Embeddings are built locally at compile time using ONNX Runtime. The client uses hybrid BM25 keyword scoring and cosine similarity.
search.feature.hybrid.title: Hybrid Re-ranking
search.feature.hybrid.desc: Combines fast BM25 keyword matching with vector similarity for the absolute best search relevance and speed.
search.models.title: Supported Embedding Models
search.models.sub: Select the perfect embedding model tailored for your documentation size and languages.
search.models.alert: 💡 Multilingual documentation: If your documentation website contains multiple languages (such as English, Chinese, German, Spanish, etc.), select a multilingual model using docmd-search --settings. The default model is English-only and will produce poor search relevance for other languages.
search.cli.title: Easy Command Line Integration
search.cli.sub: Build your local index and preview the search relevance in seconds.
search.api.title: Pure-Client API: Build Custom UIs
search.api.sub: Integrate offline vector search into any custom frontend framework, independent of docmd.
search.api.desc1: An ultra-lightweight client runtime (<5KB minified) that executes entirely in the browser using hybrid BM25 and vector cosine similarity scoring.
search.faq.title: Search Frequently Asked Questions
search.faq.sub: Everything you need to know about docmd offline semantic search.
search.faq.q1: Does docmd search run entirely client-side?
search.faq.a1:
Yes. The search runtime performs all vector similarity calculations and keyword indexing directly in the user's browser. It requires zero cloud infrastructure or search APIs.

Read docmd-search documentation →
search.faq.q2: Are ONNX model weights downloaded on every visit?
search.faq.a2:
No. Model weights are only loaded during compilation/build time using Node.js to generate static search vector indices. The client-side runtime only downloads the pre-built indices, which are compressed JSON chunks.

Learn how offline search works →
search.faq.q3: Can I use the search plugin with multiple languages?
search.faq.a3:
Yes. If your documentation is multilingual, you should choose a multilingual embedding model like paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 which supports over 50 languages.

Learn about multi-language search models →
search.faq.q4: What is showConfidence and how does it work?
search.faq.a4:
The showConfidence flag, when enabled, displays the exact similarity matching percentage badge next to each semantic result, helping users visually understand search relevance.

Read about browser-client settings →

faq.q8: What are docmd Agent Skills (SKILL.md) and how do I install them?
faq.a8:
docmd supports SKILL.md manifests so AI coding agents (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf) can read and execute documentation tasks automatically. Install official skills into your workspace using:
npx docmd-skills [target-directory]
